subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class pre-compaction warning, structured handoff, and bounded deferral semantics to core compaction, and what authority must survive or expire across that boundary?
rationale: Current source shows the requested lifecycle is missing, but implementing it adds public config, session-state, and security/authority behavior that repository policy treats as maintainer-owned product and security design.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Approve a core design that specifies warning thresholds, one bounded handoff turn, checkpoint fields, deferral limits, audit logs, and resume authority validation before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Hooks
options.body: Keep core surfaces as hooks plus notifyUser, memoryFlush, and checkpoints, and ask for plugin or hook-pack implementations until a missing core API is proven.

options.title: Defer New Compaction Surface
options.body: Leave the issue open but do not implement new config or deferral semantics until a maintainer-sponsored design chooses the security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a core design that specifies warning thresholds, one bounded handoff turn, checkpoint fields, deferral limits, audit logs, and resume authority validation before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent compaction config, schema, hook, and checkpoint history points to vincentkoc as the best current routing candidate for the design decision.
